name: California
summary: A white field with a grizzly bear walking on a patch of grass, a red star in the upper hoist, a red stripe along the bottom and the words 'CALIFORNIA REPUBLIC'. It is based on the flag of the 1846 Bear Flag Revolt.
origin: In June 1846, American settlers revolted against Mexican rule in Sonoma and raised a homemade flag with a bear, a star and 'California Republic', drawn by William L. Todd. The 'republic' lasted about 25 days before the US took control in the Mexican–American War.
The legislature adopted the bear flag in 1911. A 1953 law standardised the design; the bear is said to be modelled on Monarch, the last captive California grizzly.

symbols.name: Grizzly bear
symbols.description: A brown grizzly walking toward the hoist.
symbols.meaning: Strength and independence; the California grizzly is now extinct.

symbols.name: Red star
symbols.description: A five-pointed star in the upper hoist.
symbols.meaning: Echoes the Texas lone star; sovereignty.

facts: The California grizzly, shown on the flag, has been extinct since the 1920s.
The original 1846 flag was destroyed in the fires after the 1906 San Francisco earthquake.
It is one of the best-known US state flags worldwide.
clues: A grizzly bear on white with a red star and the words 'CALIFORNIA REPUBLIC'.
Based on the flag of a 25-day republic in 1846.
The animal on it is extinct in the wild in the state.
